brief:
Banks have begun freezing accounts belonging to sanctioned Israeli companies operating in the West Bank, according to Middle East Eye, even before the British punitive measures officially take effect. The early action demonstrates how financial institutions are preemptively responding to the impending sanctions regime.

The move reflects growing pressure on banks to distance themselves from entities involved in West Bank operations ahead of Britain's formal implementation of the sanctions. The freezing of accounts signals banks' efforts to avoid potential violations or regulatory complications once the measures formally commence.

title: British sanctions freeze Israeli company accounts in West Bank
